What voters are considering

One proposal, multiple district needs.

USD 329 is proposing general obligation bonds to construct and equip a new Career and Technical Education facility and complete priority improvements across district schools and facilities. Final layouts, quantities and allocations remain subject to professional design, site evaluation, code review and competitive bidding.

01

Maintain

Protect existing facilities through roofing, windows, masonry, HVAC and other building-system work.

02

Improve

Update safety, security, classrooms, restrooms, kitchens, learning spaces and campus circulation.

03

Prepare

Create hands-on career learning space for welding/construction ag, electrical, plumbing and digital production pathways.

Public accountability

Accountability voters can verify.

If the bond is authorized, the district’s responsibility is to make major decisions, contracts, expenditures and material scope changes visible to the public.

Public commitments

  • Maintain a published project list.
  • Track contracts, expenditures and remaining bond funds separately.
  • Consider major contracts and material scope changes publicly.
  • Explain material changes in writing.
  • Publish design, bidding and construction progress reports.
  • Include bond activity in district audit and final accounting.

What is not yet decided

  • Final building dimensions and floor plans
  • Exact placement and orientation of new work
  • Final brands, models, materials and finishes
  • Final quantities of each improvement
  • Construction sequencing and completion dates
  • Final allocations among authorized projects
The governing principle

Plans may be responsibly refined. Unrelated projects may not be quietly substituted. Material changes should be explained publicly and remain within the voter-authorized purpose.

Fair questions

Know what the vote would—and would not—decide.

What would approval authorize?

Approval would authorize USD 329 to issue up to $14 million in general obligation bonds for the purposes described in the controlling ballot and legal documents.

Are the 3D model and renderings final architectural plans?

No. They are planning concepts intended to help people understand possible relationships and uses. Final design requires architecture, engineering, site evaluation, code review and competitive bidding.

Does the bond pay for ordinary district operating expenses?

The proposal is for capital facility purposes described in the bond documents. Voters should review the final ballot language and official district materials for the controlling authorization.

Where can I verify the official information?

Review the district’s official Bond Information Center and the final ballot/legal documents. This working site should never replace those controlling sources.
